Mortgage protection insurance: how it works and what to compare

Mortgage protection is life insurance bought so your family can pay off the home loan, or keep paying it, if you die. It is usually a term policy that you own, with the benefit paid to the person you name. This page explains how it differs from the mortgage insurance a lender may require and what to compare before you buy.

What mortgage protection is

It is a life insurance policy sized to your mortgage. You choose an amount close to what you owe and a term close to the years left on the loan. If you die while the policy is in force, the insurer pays the benefit to your beneficiary, who can use it to pay off the loan, keep up the payments or cover anything else the household needs.

You own the policy. It is not part of the loan and the lender is not a party to it.

It is not the mortgage insurance your lender asks for

Private mortgage insurance, or PMI, is a different product. The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau puts it this way: “PMI protects the lender—not you—if you stop making payments on your loan.” A lender may require PMI on a conventional loan when the down payment is less than 20 percent of the purchase price (CFPB, reviewed November 2026).

PMI does nothing for your family if you die. Mortgage protection does nothing for the lender if you stop paying. They solve different problems, and having one tells you nothing about whether you need the other.

FHA and VA loans have their own versions. Like PMI, they protect the lender, not you. Here is how they line up:

CoverageWho it protectsRequired?
Private mortgage insurance (PMI), conventional loansThe lender, if you stop making payments.A lender may require it when the down payment is under 20 percent.
FHA mortgage insuranceThe lender. If the owner defaults, FHA pays the lender a claim for the unpaid principal balance.Yes, on all FHA loans. The premiums are paid to FHA.
VA-backed loan and funding feeThe lender. VA’s backing takes the place of mortgage insurance and works in a similar way.No monthly mortgage insurance. A one-time funding fee applies unless you are exempt, for example if you receive VA compensation for a service-connected disability.
Mortgage protection (term life you own)Your family. It pays the beneficiary you name if you die during the term.No. It is optional.

Sources: CFPB on mortgage insurance, reviewed August 2026; HUD, FHA history; VA.gov funding fee page, updated October 5, 2026.

Mortgage life insurance, mortgage protection and credit life: what the names mean

These names get mixed up, and they can describe two different kinds of coverage.

  • A term life policy you own. This is what this page calls mortgage protection. You choose the amount and the term, and the benefit goes to the person you name.
  • Credit life insurance. This is sold with a loan to pay off some or all of the debt if you die. The National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC) says the proceeds are “paid directly to the creditor,” which means the lender, not your family.

“Mortgage life insurance” can mean either one. The NAIC also says that, apart from private mortgage insurance, a lender cannot deny you credit because you do not buy optional credit insurance (NAIC, updated January 2024). The questions below help you tell which kind you are being offered.

Questions to ask about any coverage offered with a loan

Some coverage is sold alongside the mortgage itself. Before you accept it, ask:

  • Who receives the benefit? Your family, or the lender.
  • Does the benefit shrink as the loan balance falls, while the premium stays the same?
  • Does it end if you refinance, sell or move?
  • Can the premium change during the term?

Then compare the answers with a term life policy that you own.

Got a letter about mortgage protection after your closing? See what to check before you answer it.

Is mortgage protection worth it?

It depends on the coverage you already have. Start with three numbers: what you owe on the home, the years left on the loan, and the life insurance you already carry, including any through work.

If what you have would pay off the loan and still leave enough for your family to live on, a new policy may add little. If there is a gap, a term policy sized to the loan is one way to fill it.

If you are offered coverage that is tied to the loan, price a term policy first. The NAIC gives the same advice about credit insurance: check what traditional term life would cost, because you may find it costs less (NAIC).

What to compare

  • Term length. Match it to the years left on the mortgage, or longer if others will still depend on your income.
  • Level or decreasing benefit. A level benefit stays the same for the whole term. A decreasing benefit falls over time.
  • Riders. Some policies can add features such as a waiver of premium if you become disabled. They vary by carrier and state.
  • Conversion. Some term policies can be converted to permanent coverage without new health questions, within a time limit.
  • Underwriting. Some policies ask health questions with no medical exam. Others require an exam. Which one fits depends on your age, your health and the amount.

How long mortgage protection lasts

It lasts for the term you choose, for example the years left on the loan. As long as the premiums are paid, it stays in force to the end of that term, even if you pay the loan off early.

Virginia’s State Corporation Commission explains that if you live past the term, the policy expires with no value and pays no benefit. Some term policies can be renewed when the term ends, though the insurer may charge a new premium based on your age at renewal. Some can be converted to a permanent policy before the term ends (Virginia Consumer’s Guide for Life Insurance).

Does mortgage protection cover job loss?

No. Mortgage protection is life insurance. It pays a death benefit. It does not make your loan payments if you lose your job.

Losing income to an illness or injury is a different risk. Disability income insurance is built for that.

Some lenders offer credit involuntary unemployment insurance, a separate, optional product. The NAIC says it pays a set number of monthly loan payments to the lender if you lose your job through no fault of your own (NAIC).

Buying mortgage protection after 60

You can still apply. Age limits, and the term lengths offered at each age, vary by carrier, so a term that runs to the end of a long loan may not be available. Price also rises with age. The NAIC notes that life insurance becomes more expensive as you get older (NAIC).

If the loan is close to paid off and your main concern is funeral costs and final bills, a smaller final expense policy may fit your needs instead.

Veterans with a mortgage: VA runs its own program, Veterans’ Mortgage Life Insurance (VMLI). It is for service members and veterans who have a severe disability that VA has found was caused or made worse by their service, received a Specially Adapted Housing grant, hold title to the home, have a mortgage on it and are under 70. VMLI pays up to $200,000 directly to the lender. It is decreasing-term coverage and ends when the mortgage is paid off. Details and how to apply are on VA.gov (page updated June 4, 2025). Honorbrook is not connected with VA. If VMLI does not apply to you, a term policy you own can be sized to the loan. See life insurance for veterans.

What sets the price

Each carrier prices a policy on the applicant’s own details. Virginia’s Bureau of Insurance says premiums depend largely on the type of policy and on your health, age, gender, occupation, family health history and lifestyle (Virginia SCC, September 2023). Carriers also ask whether you use tobacco. For mortgage protection, the amount, the length of the term, a level or decreasing benefit and any riders you add also count.

We do not publish sample prices because a price that is not based on your own details is not useful. After a short conversation we can show you real figures from the carriers that fit.

Common questions

Mortgage protection questions

Is mortgage protection insurance required?
No. It is optional life insurance. It is different from private mortgage insurance, which a lender can require on a conventional loan with a down payment under 20 percent and which protects the lender.
Do I need it if I already have life insurance?
Maybe not. If the coverage you have is enough to pay the mortgage and cover your other needs, a separate policy may be unnecessary. We look at both before recommending anything.
What happens to the policy if I refinance or move?
A life insurance policy that you own is not tied to the loan. It stays in force as long as the premiums are paid, whichever lender or home you have.
Can I qualify with health problems?
It depends on the carrier, the condition and the amount. Some policies ask health questions with no medical exam and others require an exam. We check which carriers fit your situation before you apply.
Who receives the money?
The beneficiary you name on the policy. They decide how to use it, whether that is paying off the loan, keeping up the payments or something else.
What is mortgage life insurance?
Life insurance meant to pay off a home loan, or keep up the payments, if you die. The name is used for two different things: a term policy you own, which pays the person you name, and credit life sold with a loan, which pays the lender. Ask which one you are being offered.
Is mortgage protection insurance worth it?
It depends on the coverage you already have. Compare what you owe and what your family would need with the life insurance you already carry. If there is a gap, price a term policy you own before you accept coverage tied to the loan.
How long does mortgage protection insurance last?
For the term you choose, as long as the premiums are paid. If you outlive the term, the policy ends and pays nothing. Some policies can be renewed, and the insurer may charge a new premium based on your age then. Some can be converted to permanent coverage before the term ends.
Does mortgage protection insurance cover job loss?
No. It is life insurance and pays a death benefit. Disability income insurance is built for income lost to an illness or injury. Some lenders offer separate, optional credit involuntary unemployment insurance that makes a set number of loan payments to the lender.
Can I buy mortgage protection after 60?
You can apply. Age limits and the term lengths offered at each age vary by carrier, and the price rises with age. If the loan is nearly paid off and your concern is final costs, a smaller final expense policy may fit instead.
Does VA offer mortgage protection for veterans?
VA offers Veterans’ Mortgage Life Insurance (VMLI) to service members and veterans with a severe service-connected disability who received a Specially Adapted Housing grant, hold title to the home, have a mortgage on it and are under 70. It pays up to $200,000 to the lender, per VA.gov (updated June 4, 2025). Honorbrook is not connected with VA. Other veterans can consider term coverage they own.
